sillida_evidence: Sillida's full territory and Pulau Cingkuak are ceded to VOC by the rulers of Bajang, Indrapura, and Trosang -- none of them Sillida-native
representation_result: Represented as three separate RECOGNIZES_OFFICE_HOLDER relations (one per ceding ruler, each -> VOC), dated 1667 and reconfirmed 1681, with claim_or_effective_control=FORMAL_ACCEPTANCE, never a sovereignty-implying value
workaround_prohibited: Did not invent a CEDES_TERRITORY_TO or TRANSFERS_SOVEREIGNTY relation type (forbidden); did not merge the three ceding rulers into one actor
notes: RECOGNIZES_OFFICE_HOLDER (VOC as the recognized authority) proved sufficient to represent the cession act without a dedicated territory-transfer relation type.

ontology_component: Absence of native Sillida ruler's voice
sillida_evidence: Sillida's own regents are not parties to either the 1667 cession or its 1681 reconfirmation -- the ceding parties are three neighboring rulers throughout
representation_result: No native-Sillida-ruler actor was invented to fill this gap; ACTOR_SILLIDA_REGENTS is modeled only where the source itself documents their presence (1679 fine-recipient, 1698 toll-relinquishment), explicitly NOT asserted to have had standing in 1667/1681
workaround_prohibited: Did not fabricate a Sillida-native ruler or assume the 1679/1698 regents represent the same body that would have had standing in 1667/1681
notes: Validator check 13 mechanically confirms no fabricated native-ruler actor exists; check 15 confirms the absence itself is documented, not silently passed over.

sillida_evidence: The source never establishes the legal basis on which Bajang, Indrapura, and Trosang's rulers could cede Sillida's own territory
representation_result: ACTOR_SULTHAN_ACHMET_CHIA_BAJANG (and the other two ceding rulers)' own mandate_status fields explicitly flag this as an unresolved authority question, researcher_review_required=true
workaround_prohibited: Did not assume the neighboring rulers' claimed authority was legitimate or illegitimate -- both possibilities are left open
proposed_future_review: Recommend a future source check for any independent evidence of a suzerainty relationship between Bajang/Indrapura/Trosang and Sillida predating 1667
notes: Directly reuses the frozen ledger's own explicit note (field 25): 'raising an unresolved question this report does not answer.'

sillida_evidence: Armed conflict over the Soengai Kepahian gold vein boundary, resolved by a VOC-imposed peace treaty and fine
representation_result: CONTESTS_RESOURCE_WITH(Bajang's 1679 ruler, Sillida's regents) represents the underlying dispute with two determinable endpoints; VOC's own adjudicating/fine-collecting role is recorded only in notes, not as its own relation
workaround_prohibited: Did not invent a relation type for 'imposes and collects a punitive fine as third-party arbitrator'; did not stretch COLLECTS_TOLL_FROM to represent a one-time fine (which is not an ongoing toll)
proposed_future_review: Recommend a future Draft V2 revision consider whether a dedicated relation type or an annotation sub-field is warranted for third-party arbitration/fine outcomes, distinct from both toll collection (recurring) and military force (direct combatant action)
notes: VOC's own disproportionate 600-of-1000-rijksdaalder fine share (three times Sillida's own 200) is recorded in relation notes only, since no relation type captures third-party arbitration outcomes.

sillida_evidence: A specific, named gold vein straddling the Bayang-Sillida boundary, discovered after 1667 and prompting the 1681 reconfirmation
representation_result: Modeled as its own object, LOCATION_SOENGAI_KEPAHIAN_GOLD_VEIN, distinct from LOCATION_SILLIDA_MINE (the established mine) and from LOCATION_SILLIDA (the wider territory)
workaround_prohibited: Did not conflate the disputed boundary vein with the established mine or the wider territory
notes: Confirms Draft V2's Location entity model can support a resource-boundary-specific object distinct from both the settlement and the operational mine site.

sillida_evidence: Sillida's (and jointly Padang's) regents relinquish a long-held hereditary 'salimoet' toll right they had enjoyed from VOC, tied to a renegotiated pepper price
representation_result: The standing right itself is represented via COLLECTS_TOLL_FROM(Sillida regents, VOC) in the SOURCE-SUPPORTED direction (regents as beneficiary), with valid_to marking the 1698 relinquishment date; the relinquishment ACT itself has no dedicated relation type
workaround_prohibited: Did not reverse COLLECTS_TOLL_FROM's own direction to mean 'relinquishes'; did not invent a RELINQUISHES_RIGHT_TO relation type
proposed_future_review: Recommend the same future review flagged for Tiku V3's T-04 (toll exemption) -- this is a structurally identical gap: Draft V2 has no relation type for voluntarily surrendering a previously-held right, only for holding or claiming one
notes: Directly parallel, cross-case-corroborating finding to Tiku V3's own T-04 (1641 toll exemption) -- the SAME underlying gap (no relation type for rights EXEMPTIONS or RELINQUISHMENTS, only for rights HELD or CLAIMED) now appears in a third form.

sillida_evidence: VOC leases the loss-making Salido mine's operation to Radja Nanxatti for a fee, rent, and fixed gold price, while 'expressly maintaining its sovereignty rights'
representation_result: LEASES_RESOURCE_TO(VOC, Radja Nanxatti) represents the operational grant; the source's own explicit sovereignty-retention statement is represented via a SEPARATE CLAIMS_JURISDICTION_OVER(VOC, mine location) relation
workaround_prohibited: Did not fold the sovereignty retention into the lease relation itself, which would have obscured the source's own deliberate separation of the two
notes: The artifact's cleanest claim-vs-effective-control demonstration: the source ITSELF states the separation VOC intended, and Draft V2's own vocabulary (LEASES_RESOURCE_TO plus CLAIMS_JURISDICTION_OVER) represents it without strain.

sillida_evidence: Painan's own ruler voluntarily cedes land specifically to secure the overland route connecting the Sillida mine to coastal shipping
representation_result: Represented via its own RECOGNIZES_OFFICE_HOLDER relation (Sultan Sampourna -> VOC), explicitly contrasted in notes with the Sillida cessions (external rulers ceding Sillida's own land) as a case where the ceding party IS the land's own acknowledged ruler
workaround_prohibited: Did not merge this relation with the Sillida cession relations despite topical proximity (both secure mine-related territory)
notes: Confirms the artifact can hold two structurally different cession-mandate patterns (external-ruler cession vs. self-cession) side by side without forcing one interpretation onto both.

ontology_component: Claim versus effective control (mine jurisdiction vs. operation)
sillida_evidence: VOC's sovereignty claim over the mine (1737) is explicitly separated from Radja Nanxatti's practical operational control
representation_result: REL_1737_CLAIMS_JURISDICTION_MINE (claim_or_effective_control=CLAIM) and REL_1737_LEASES_MINE (claim_or_effective_control=COMMERCIAL_CONTROL) carry two distinct values for the same underlying resource
workaround_prohibited: Did not homogenize the two dimensions into one relation or one control value
notes: Validator check 26 mechanically confirms this distinction holds.

sillida_evidence: A company of enslaved persons from the Sillida mine is deployed as an armed auxiliary in two 1687 operations (the Radja doa Selas capture and the Batoe Bannaw expedition)
representation_result: Represented ONLY as a standalone observation (OBS_CONSTRAINED_AGENCY_ARMED_ENSLAVED_COMPANY), never as a relation -- the company never appears as subject or object of any relation anywhere in the artifact
workaround_prohibited: Did not create ENSLAVES, COMMANDS_SLAVE_COMPANY, ALLY_OF, or VOLUNTARILY_SUPPORTS (all forbidden); did not force the company into an existing relation type (e.g. USES_MILITARY_FORCE_AGAINST) that would misstate either their own coerced status or VOC's command relationship
proposed_future_review: Recommend a future Draft V2 revision consider a dedicated first-class or annotation-level 'CommandRelationship' construct for coerced/constrained-agency labor deployed under military command, distinct from both a voluntary alliance and a punitive military-force relation
notes: This is the artifact's central, and most significant, ontology failure: Draft V2 provides NO way to represent a command-over-coerced-labor relationship as a directed relation without either inventing forbidden vocabulary or fundamentally mischaracterizing the relationship's own nature. The observation-only workaround preserves the finding but does not resolve the representational gap.

ontology_component: Command relationship and constrained agency (structured observation)
sillida_evidence: The same armed enslaved company's deployment is documented in two dated operations one month apart
representation_result: OBS_CONSTRAINED_AGENCY_ARMED_ENSLAVED_COMPANY carries claim_or_effective_control=ADMINISTRATIVE_CONTROL for VOC's own command authority over deployment, explicitly NOT characterizing the company's own political stance
workaround_prohibited: Did not use claim_or_effective_control to imply the company's own consent or resistance -- only VOC's command authority is characterized by that field
notes: Confirms Draft V2's EffectiveControlObservation entity (already used for Natal's 1712 compliance and Koto Tangah's destruction years) extends to a command-relationship use case, even though it cannot fully resolve T-10's own relation-type gap.

sillida_evidence: No source documents the armed enslaved company's own loyalty, voluntary collaboration, or resistance
representation_result: OBS_CONSTRAINED_AGENCY_ARMED_ENSLAVED_COMPANY's own interpretive_status=CANNOT_DETERMINE, reused directly from the frozen ledger's own row-118/126 finding
workaround_prohibited: Did not default to either a loyalty or resistance reading in the absence of evidence
notes: Direct reuse of an already-completed batch finding, not re-derived -- validator check 22 confirms this value is present.

ontology_component: Colonial punitive classification (VOC's 'rebellie' framing) as annotation only
sillida_evidence: VOC's 1679 peace treaty labels Bayang's gold-vein incursion 'bedrevene rebellie' (committed rebellion) despite the dispute being local-vs-local over a resource boundary
representation_result: The label is recorded in relation notes/theoretical_annotation only; no relation_type anywhere in the artifact encodes 'rebellion' or any punitive classification
workaround_prohibited: Did not create a REBELS_AGAINST relation type (forbidden) or otherwise promote VOC's own classificatory language into the controlled relation vocabulary
notes: Directly operationalizes Draft V2's own demotion of IMPOSES_PUNITIVE_CLASSIFICATION_ON to annotation-only (per the cross-case review), consistent with every prior case in this project.

sillida_evidence: The full episode spans territorial cession, boundary dispute, mine lease, sovereignty claim, and toll relinquishment -- a genuinely multi-relation-type resource-governance case
representation_result: Six distinct relation types are used across 14 relations (RECOGNIZES_OFFICE_HOLDER x7, CONTESTS_RESOURCE_WITH x2, LEASES_RESOURCE_TO x1, CLAIMS_JURISDICTION_OVER x1, USES_MILITARY_FORCE_AGAINST x2, COLLECTS_TOLL_FROM x1)
workaround_prohibited: Did not force the whole episode into a single relation type for simplicity
notes: Confirms Draft V2's MVP_CORE relation set is rich enough to represent a genuinely multi-dimensional resource-governance case without a dedicated 'resource governance bundle' construct.

ontology_component: Spatial ambiguity (mine vs. territory vs. related locations)
sillida_evidence: Sources use 'Sillida'/'Salido' for the wider territory, the mine specifically, and sometimes the settlement interchangeably; Painan, Pulau Cingkuak, and Batoe Bannaw are all named separately
representation_result: Six distinct Location entities are modeled (LOCATION_SILLIDA, LOCATION_SILLIDA_MINE, LOCATION_PULAU_CINGKUAK, LOCATION_PAINAN, LOCATION_SOENGAI_KEPAHIAN_GOLD_VEIN, LOCATION_BATOE_BANNAW), each used only where the source's own context supports the distinction
workaround_prohibited: Did not collapse all Sillida-area place references into one location entity for simplicity, which would have obscured the mine-vs-territory claim/control test (T-09)
proposed_future_review: Recommend a future check on whether LOCATION_SILLIDA and LOCATION_SILLIDA_MINE are ALWAYS cleanly distinguishable in the underlying sources, or whether some rows use 'Sillida' ambiguously between the two (a genuine, not yet fully resolved, spatial-precision question)
notes: The most granular location model of any of this project's four validation cases -- directly enabled by, and enabling, the claim/control separation test (T-09).

sillida_evidence: 'sulthan Achmet Chia' (1667, 1681) and 'sulthan Niamoelia' (1679) both hold the office of Bajang's ruler at different points, 12 years apart
representation_result: Modeled as two separate actors (ACTOR_SULTHAN_ACHMET_CHIA_BAJANG, ACTOR_SULTHAN_NIAMOELIA_BAJANG), explicitly not merged, with no invented succession chain connecting them
workaround_prohibited: Did not assume Achmet Chia and Niamoelia are the same person under two names, or invent a succession narrative the source does not supply
notes: A NEW office-holder-succession test not present in prior cases -- confirms the office/office-holder separation discipline extends cleanly to same-office-different-holder situations across time.

ontology_component: Actor continuity across the full 1648-1740s span
sillida_evidence: 'Sillida' is named across at least 8 dated points spanning roughly a century
representation_result: No single 'ACTOR_SILLIDA_1648_1740' bridging construct was created; ACTOR_SILLIDA_REGENTS itself is deliberately NOT asserted to persist continuously (only two dated appearances, 19 years apart, explicitly not bridged to the earlier absent-voice period)
workaround_prohibited: Did not invent a persisting Sillida political actor across the full span, per the same discipline established in Koto Tangah V2 and Tiku V3
notes: Consistent with the now-established cross-case pattern (Koto Tangah T-14, Tiku T-12) -- this artifact avoids even attempting a full-span bridge, though it does note the field limitation (no continuity_status is Draft V2-native) is the same underlying gap.

ontology_component: Patron-client annotation (no edge despite fine-sharing and mine dependency)
sillida_evidence: VOC collects the largest share of the 1679 fine, retains sovereignty while leasing operational control (1737), and jointly negotiates the 1698 toll relinquishment with Sillida's regents
representation_result: patron_client_classification is PATRON_CLIENT_NOT_TESTABLE on every relation in this artifact -- no dyad is classified as patron-client despite the recurring asymmetric-benefit pattern
workaround_prohibited: Did not classify the VOC-Sillida relationship as patron-client merely because VOC repeatedly captures disproportionate value
notes: Fourth consecutive case (after Painan, Natal, Koto Tangah, Tiku) where the patron-client hard rule holds under a genuinely asymmetric, resource-extraction-heavy relationship.

ontology_component: Temporal gaps and no continuous-control interpolation
sillida_evidence: Large gaps exist between 1648, 1667/1681, 1679, 1687, 1698, and 1737 -- roughly a century of intermittent documentation
representation_result: No relation or observation was fabricated to fill any gap; each relation's own valid_from/valid_to remain bounded to its own dated episode, and no single relation spans the whole 1648-1737+ period
workaround_prohibited: Did not assume continuous VOC administrative control, continuous Sillida-regent presence, or continuous anything across any of the multi-decade gaps
notes: Confirms the temporal-gap discipline established in Koto Tangah V2 and Tiku V3 extends cleanly to a case with even sparser, more irregular documentation.

ontology_component: Public-copy restraint (no raw classificatory language leaking to public display)
sillida_evidence: Source language includes 'bedrevene rebellie' (committed rebellion), 'Sclaven' (slaves), and 'aufs neue abtrünnig' (renewed defector)
representation_result: Every public_display_summary field paraphrases the underlying action neutrally, without reproducing VOC's own punitive or dehumanizing classificatory language verbatim
workaround_prohibited: Did not put 'rebellion,' 'renewed defector,' or any similarly loaded VOC classification directly into a public_display_summary field
notes: Confirms Draft V2 section 9's own public-display guard holds for a fourth case, including one involving enslaved persons -- the term 'Sclaven' itself is preserved only in source_statement_summary/notes (as the source's own diplomatically-preserved term, per the frozen ledger's own explicit instruction), never in public_display_summary.
